{"description":"Opening a design written under a vocabulary this binary does not know ends in one of two states: the reader is told precisely what it lacks, or the open is refused. It never succeeds quietly and then shows less than the file holds.

⭐ BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-09-12 (epoch:planned-a-vocabulary-change-is-never-silent). The stamp now records every enum vocabulary the schema declares, keyed Type.property, beside the type names it already carried. On open the guard compares them and refuses — naming the value — only when the graph actually STORES a value this binary does not know; a value merely declared and unused opens, the rule bought with two lockouts. Every stamp written before this still parses (serde-default), and the values do not enter content_hash, so lineage is untouched.

THE MEASURED HOLE IT CLOSED, 2026-09-11: the stamp named TYPES only. Decision.status gaining `deferred` moved no count and no name, so an older binary opened the graph with no warning, compared status == "proposed", and the decision VANISHED from loop_status and what_next rather than erroring.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO, per dec:the-stamp-records-enum-values-and-nothing-finer: property additions are not recorded (frequent, low harm — an older reader shows fewer fields and can tell; recording them would make nearly every release a migration), and semantic changes are not claimed (beyond any structural fingerprint; the per-change-identity road stays open for them).

ONE HONEST LIMIT, stated in the code: no registry of REMOVED enum values exists, so the guard cannot say whether the binary is behind or the value was removed. It names both and gives the reader the two stamps' versions as the discriminator, rather than asserting the commoner case.

THE BOUND THAT ARGUED FOR IT: being told to migrate is an inconvenience, and migration has been shown lossless here (3,989 nodes and 21,555 edges in, same out). Only the SILENT case argued for any of this.","name":"A reader whose binary does not know a design's vocabulary is told what it lacks, or refused — never shown less of the design than it holds","provenance":"authored","status":"verified","tier":"operational"}
